nodes.label: VGOD Glitch Art Desktop Background
nodes.description: A wide-format background image featuring heavy glitch art aesthetics: dominant cyan/turquoise hues overlaid with purple and magenta chromatic aberration, vertical CRT scan-line distortion pattern, and a corrupted/distorted silhouette figure (animal or abstract form) rendered in the glitch style. Dark vignette border frames the composition.

nodes.label: Glitch Art Visual Aesthetic
nodes.description: The image employs deliberate digital corruption aesthetics: chromatic aberration splitting color channels, vertical scan-line interference reminiscent of CRT monitor artifacts, and pixelated color bleed. These are hallmarks of glitch art as a visual style.

nodes.label: CRT Scan-Line Distortion Pattern
nodes.description: Dark vertical lines overlay the entire image at regular intervals, simulating the scan-line pattern of a CRT display or analog video signal interference. This is a prominent and intentional retro-tech visual element.

nodes.label: Cyan-Dominant Vaporwave Color Palette
nodes.description: The image uses a vivid cyan/turquoise base with purple, magenta, and dark teal accents. This high-saturation, cool-warm contrast palette is characteristic of vaporwave and retro-futurist digital art movements.

nodes.label: Distorted Abstract Silhouette Figure
nodes.description: A dark, corrupted silhouette form occupies the center-left of the image. The glitch distortion makes its exact subject ambiguous — it could be an animal (goose-related given project context), a human figure, or a purely abstract shape. The distortion intentionally obscures the original subject.

nodes.label: Retro-Chaos Desktop Atmosphere Intent
nodes.description: The aggressive glitch aesthetic of this background image is likely chosen to complement the Win95-style desktop environment of GooseOS, amplifying its retro-chaos personality. The corruption and scan-line effects create a sense of digital irreverence that matches the project's playful, lo-fi brand.

nodes.label: Background Named After Visual/Cultural Reference (vgod)
nodes.description: The filename 'vgod' may reference 'vape god' (internet/meme culture), a gaming handle, or a creative alias, suggesting the background images in GooseOS are named after cultural references or creator identities rather than descriptive content — an informal, community-driven asset naming convention.

nodes.label: Dark Vignette Border Framing
nodes.description: A dark border or vignette frames the edges of the image, drawing focus to the glitched center and giving the background a contained, monitor-screen-within-a-monitor feeling — reinforcing the retro CRT display metaphor.
